Here's how I'd run this onboarding check against the Simulator that's already running. It reads the accessibility tree instead of taking screenshots, and it doesn't reinstall, reset, or clear data. I haven't run anything yet, so there are no results below. The commands use placeholders until I resolve them on your machine.

## 1. Identify the target and app (read-only)

```sh
xcrun simctl list -j devices booted          # take the UDID of the booted device
flutter devices                               # confirm Flutter sees the same UDID
xcrun simctl get_app_container <UDID> <staging-bundle-id> app
```

- I'll get the staging bundle identifier from the Xcode staging scheme or build configuration. I won't guess it from the Dart package name.
- I'll record the Simulator as **reused, not created for this task**. That means cleanup only covers files I create.
- If onboarding has already been completed on this install, the app will open past it. In that case I'll stop and ask you before uninstalling, clearing app data, or erasing the Simulator.

## 2. Read the tree instead of taking screenshots

I'll use `idb` only if it's already installed or you approve it. If the Dart and Flutter MCP server is connected to the running staging session, its widget inspection is an equivalent read-only option.

```sh
idb ui describe-all --udid <UDID> --json \
  | jq '[.[] | select(.AXLabel or .AXUniqueId) |
        {type, label: .AXLabel, id: .AXUniqueId, enabled, frame}]'
```

The filtered output is a few hundred tokens per screen. I'll keep that summary, not the raw dump.

**If the tree is empty** (a single full-screen Flutter view, or no actionable nodes):
1. Make sure the app is in the foreground and past the splash screen, then read again after a short wait.
2. This usually means semantics isn't enabled. The fix is a debug or automation entrypoint that calls `SemanticsBinding.instance.ensureSemantics()`, never the production entry path. That requires relaunching staging with a different `-t`, so I'd ask you first. As a last resort I could use coordinates, and I'd say so in the report.

## 3. Walk the three screens: act, then re-read

For each onboarding screen:

1. Confirm the screen from its distinctive node: an identifier if one exists, otherwise its title label or page indicator.
2. Find the advance control ("Next" / "Continue" / "Get started") by `AXUniqueId`, then by exact label, then by role and index.
3. Tap the center of its frame: `idb ui tap --udid <UDID> <x> <y>`.
4. Re-read the tree, retrying for a few seconds at most, until the next screen's node appears. A tap command exiting with code 0 only proves the event was sent.

After screen 3, the check passes when the tree shows the **sign-in screen**: its heading plus the email/password fields or sign-in button. I'll assert on those nodes, not on the absence of onboarding nodes.

Details I'll watch for:
- Buttons and `ListTile`s merge their child labels, so I'll match on the joined label.
- A `PageView` only exposes pages it has built, so I'll re-read after each transition instead of searching ahead.

## 4. Evidence and cleanup

- **Logs:** a short capture filtered to the app, started before the first tap:
  ```sh
  xcrun simctl spawn <UDID> log stream --predicate 'process == "Runner"'
  ```
- **Screenshot:** at most one, of the final sign-in screen, using `xcrun simctl io <UDID> screenshot <task-path>.png`, cropped or downscaled. The tree reads are the main evidence.
- **Cleanup:** stop the log stream and delete only the files I created. I won't change permissions, appearance, status bar, or app data.

## Report you'll get

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Target | iOS Simulator (reused), device model + iOS runtime |
| Build | staging flavor, as already launched (debug mode unless shown otherwise) |
| Entrypoint | existing session's entrypoint; I'll note it if a semantics-enabled entrypoint was needed |
| Data source | staging backend, though onboarding is likely local-only |
| Flow | onboarding 1 → 2 → 3 → sign-in |
| Assertions | node found per screen, sign-in nodes present |
| Artifacts | filtered tree summaries, one screenshot, filtered log excerpt |
| Not exercised | onboarding Back/skip paths, a fresh install's first-run state (if the existing data already reflects it), physical-device behavior, any native permission prompts |

**Before I run it:** is `idb` (or the Dart/Flutter MCP server) available? If not, do you approve installing `idb` for this check? If you'd like this to become a durable check, the next step is a `package:integration_test` smoke test that uses `Semantics(identifier:)` on the onboarding buttons. That's outside what you asked for here, so I'd only do it if you want it.

with_skill.response:
You can tap by coordinates to unblock the smoke run. The tap's exit code won't tell you whether Pay worked, though, so you'll need to check the result yourself.

**Before tapping Pay:** make sure this build uses a test or sandbox payment backend and a test account. A coordinate tap is blind, and it could submit a real charge.

### Tap by position

```sh
# Confirm the checkout screen is in the foreground and settled
adb -s <serial> exec-out screencap -p > /tmp/checkout-before.png

# Screencap pixels match input coordinates; check for any size override
adb -s <serial> shell wm size
```

Find the center of the Pay button on the full-resolution screenshot, not a downscaled preview. Then tap:

```sh
adb -s <serial> shell input tap <x> <y>
```

### Verify that it did something

You can't re-read an empty tree, so check the outcome another way within a bounded wait:

```sh
adb -s <serial> exec-out screencap -p > /tmp/checkout-after.png
adb -s <serial> logcat -d -s flutter | tail -n 50
```

Confirm that the confirmation or processing screen appeared, or that the expected log line fired. If nothing changed, don't retry blindly. The tap may have missed, or the button may have been disabled. In the smoke report, mark this step as "coordinate tap; semantics tree unavailable."

### Why the tree is empty

This usually doesn't mean the button lacks semantics. Flutter often builds the Android accessibility bridge only when the OS reports an assistive technology or automation client. That's why `uiautomator` sees only the `FlutterView`. If you want this step to be stable later instead of tied to coordinates:

- Use the project's `integration_test` harness, or an existing debug or automation entrypoint, that holds `SemanticsBinding.instance.ensureSemantics()`. Keep it out of the production `main`.
- Give the button a `Semantics(identifier: 'checkout-pay')`. On Android it shows up as the resource ID, so `uiautomator` can find it on any screen size.

The coordinate approach will break on a different emulator resolution, font scale, or layout change. That's fine for getting this run through, but it isn't durable for automation.
